body:
Detect runtime/doc/*.txt patches that only modify date AND modify N/A Vimscript functions as N/A.

------

## Problem:
It's not enough to detect N/A patches even I list all N/A Vimscript functions. Need to modify `xfuncname` which means modifying `.gitattributes` or passing inline config (if possible?) to detect Ex commands, options. Also, `{` is incompatible with `-I` flag so I cannot remove hunks that modify `available when compiled with` . May need many backslashes, `\`  , to ensure `{` and similar characters are escaped.

```
vim-patch:8.2.4761: documentation for using LSP messages is incomplete
vim-patch:8.2.4780: parsing an LSP message fails when it is split
vim-patch:1a946044f runtime(doc): correct return types for job_start() and job_status()
vim-patch:1cd31a450 runtime(doc): update return type for job_info()
vim-patch:15141208e runtime(doc): -x is only available when compiled with crypt feature
vim-patch:a37fd7274 runtime(doc): Remove accidental option name highlighting from :help channel.txt
vim-patch:9.2.0021: channel: connection timeout fails to fall back to IPv4
vim-patch:9.2.0314: channel: can bind to all network interfaces
vim-patch:9.2.0317: listener functions do not check secure flag
vim-patch:60e925ca0 runtime(doc): Tweak documentation style in channel.txt
vim-patch:9.2.0820: GUI: hidden popup image is displayed and not erased
vim-patch:9.2.0822: GTK4: crash menu id is null in gui_mch_destroy_menu()
vim-patch:9.2.0823: tests: Test_clientserver_servlist_list may fail
```

Vim has both json_encode() ,json_decode() but Nvim should focus on its own implementation and ignore Vim's implementation.

Far less than desired.

FYI, this specific line isn't enough to detect a new N/A patch because `{}` variant is normally 1-liner.

comment_regular_data.body:
I wish `term_` API was documented in `vim_diff` so I can just throw everything in `vim_na_hunks_vim.txt`. I can't tell how many are relevant for Neovim terminal core instead of duplicate of the Job API.

Was testing on v9.1.1110. Other files are applicable so it could be in vain.
Can't proceed without blacklisting `runtime/doc/channel.txt` but that means Vim's API for channel, job, terminal, etc. is 100% N/A in totality.

> I wish `term_` API was documented in `vim_diff` so I can just throw everything in `vim_na_hunks_vim.txt`. I can't tell how many are relevant for Neovim terminal core instead of duplicate of the Job API.

please put them all in `vim_na_hunks_vim.txt`. Vim's job/terminal stuff doesn't matter at all.

we don't need to list them in `vim_diff`. `vim_diff` is not a dictionary of every random thing vim decides to do. going forward, vim matters very little. we can use `vim_na_hunks_vim.txt` as the source of truth, but `vim_diff` is for users.

> but that means Vim's API for channel, job, terminal, etc. is 100% N/A in totality.

yup. 💯

I'll add channel.txt (and "shared" files based on filename) and do a final test run for the positive lookahead regexp before giving the 🆗 . Some patch w/ over 9000 additions (ie. version9.txt) will exceed grep's limit and falsely marked as N/A. Those patches should go to manual review until git config is adjusted for vim help files.

As for Vim/Neovim shared files/ that are incompatible, I was hesitant to mark them N/A because `builtin.txt` won't cover the majority of the API changes that could be of interest to Neovim, say 10+ years ago. Nowadays,  there's less need to rely (primarily) on vim-patch.sh for tracking which end-user Vim API to port.

We'll start with channel.txt since `terminal.txt` technically documents `:Termdebug` even if it's been ported. We'll ramp up in later PRs while revisiting C files for N/A macros.
